mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business confidence decline.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three months signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS showed sustained growth over three months.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month indicates supply-side weakness, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment turns bearish.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 70% of the instances where INDPRO declined by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market and strong economic growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where UNRATE was below 4% and PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where FEDFUNDS was above 2% and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.3% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three months signals a strong demand in the housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the broader economy benefits from increased construction activity.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where HOUST showed sustained growth over three months.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative for two consecutive quarters, it signals an economic contraction, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings decline.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where GDPC1 was negative for two consecutive quarters.
